key_insight: A closure-based ensemble adjoint model can tame chaotic backward-time growth and reveal a universal wall-stress domain of dependence in wall turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled way to infer past near-wall events from surface measurements, useful for flow sensing, reconstruction, and feedback control in high-Reynolds-number wall flows.
method: Solve adjoint Navier–Stokes equations backward in time from a wall-stress sensor kernel.
Add a linear eddy-viscosity closure in the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations to estimate the mean DOD.
Compare predicted mean DOD with ensemble-averaged adjoint fields and with the DOI from wall-stress perturbations across Reynolds numbers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the closure-based mean DOD matches ensemble averages and that both DOD and DOI show universal Reynolds-number trends, despite different spatio-temporal structures.
watch_item: Backward-time adjoint fields remain intrinsically chaotic at the realization level, so the closure captures the mean behavior but may miss sample-specific extremes or fine-scale structures.
paper_title: Mitigating adjoint chaos in wall turbulence
